title: Request Catalog Correlation — compact analytical snapshot
body:
Purpose and scope:

This is a compact working snapshot that maps recent customer asks (Q4 2029–Q1 2030) into correlated request clusters, quick-win opportunities, and tech/product risk flags. The goal is not to be exhaustive — instead, produce a tight, actionable catalog that partner teams (product, eng, optimize) can scan and act on in 30–60 minutes.

Method:
- Source inputs: support tickets, onboarding notes, CSM call transcripts, trial account audits, and two field workshops (EMEA, NA).
- Auto-clustered by semantic grouping then manually reconciled to avoid false merges (common failure: conflating "model selection" asks with "routing / fallback" asks).
- Each cluster gets: representative microstory, frequency band (low/med/high), estimated impact (qualitative), 1–2 proposed fixes (owner + size), and immediate mitigation if required.

Top-level findings (high level):
- A small number (~6) of clusters account for ~55% of high-severity asks in the window. These are concentrated around: model fallbacks & deterministic cost controls; per-route latency variability; VPC onboarding frictions; tokenization/embedding mismatches for non-English locales; billing/usage attribution granularity; and integration brittleness for server-side streaming.
- Many asks are variants of the same underlying needs: predictable unit economics and predictable quality under degraded capacity.

Cluster catalog (selection of prioritized clusters):

1) Cluster: Predictable fallback semantics and cost ceilings
- Representative microstory: "During load spikes we got routed to a larger model and costs exploded; we need a way to set hard cost ceilings per-route and graceful degraded output instead of timeouts."
- Frequency: high
- Qualitative impact: enterprise customers + PLG teams can avoid billing surprises and retention hits.
- Proposed fixes:
  - A: Per-route hard cost cap (product policy + billing enforcement). Owner: product-hosted-api. Size: M.
  - B: Degraded-output mode + structured notice in response when fallback occurs (SDK + API). Owner: eng-serving-runtime + devx. Size: S.
- Near-term mitigation: docs + templates for setting soft limits + manual routing to Dedicated.

2) Cluster: Per-request latency variance and burst handling
- Representative microstory: "We saw 95th pct latency jump 300ms for certain prompt shapes; under burst we got noisy tails and client-side retries exacerbated the problem."
- Frequency: high
- Qualitative impact: hurts interactive apps (chat UIs), increases client retries and token costs.
- Proposed fixes:
  - A: Latency SLA telemetry dashboard per-route + alerting (obs team). Owner: observability. Size: M.
  - B: Burst-aware autoscaling policy that considers KV cache warmup (infra + serving). Owner: dedicated + serving-runtime. Size: L.
- Near-term mitigation: recommended SDK retry/backoff pattern doc.

3) Cluster: VPC/onboarding friction for Private deployments
- Representative microstory: "Multiple infra handoffs, stale KMS keys, and misunderstanding about network ranges delayed POC by 3 weeks."
- Frequency: medium
- Qualitative impact: sales cycle lengthening for regulated customers.
- Proposed fixes:
  - A: One-page VPC onboarding checklist + templated CloudFormation/Terraform (solutions-eng). Owner: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services. Size: S.
  - B: Concierge onboarding pilot for top 10 deals (CS + sales). Owner: customer-success. Size: M.
- Near-term mitigation: create a "VPC readiness" intake form to be used pre-demo.

4) Cluster: Embedding/tokenization mismatches — non-English edge cases
- Representative microstory: "Embeddings for Japanese text differ significantly depending on whitespace/tokenization; search recall drops on short query variants."
- Frequency: medium
- Qualitative impact: European & APAC customers report lower dev confidence.
- Proposed fixes:
  - A: Embedding preprocessor plugin (configurable locale tokenization) + docs for common locales. Owner: eng-optimize. Size: M.
  - B: Evaluation harness and benchmark across locale-splits (research/applied-ml). Owner: applied-ml. Size: M.
- Near-term mitigation: publish locale guidance and example notebooks.

5) Cluster: Billing attribution and per-token breakdown granularity
- Representative microstory: "We can't reconcile a customer's invoice to the product routes; we need token-level attribution to route and model we used."
- Frequency: medium-high
- Qualitative impact: finance & procurement friction, renewal risk for larger accounts.
- Proposed fixes:
  - A: Add route-level and model-version labels to billing exports (finance + product). Owner: finance-and-legal + product-hosted-api. Size: S.
  - B: Self-serve billing explorer in Console (product + console-and-rollouts). Owner: product. Size: L.
- Near-term mitigation: provide tagged billing CSVs on request and better invoice line items.

6) Cluster: Server-side streaming edgecases and client integration gaps
- Representative microstory: "Client library dropped partial chunk on reconnect; developers don't have a canonical retry pattern for streamed tokens."
- Frequency: medium
- Qualitative impact: integration bugs, poor UX in chat features.
- Proposed fixes:
  - A: Streaming best-practices doc + sample resilient client patterns (devx). Owner: developer-experience. Size: S.
  - B: Small SDK change to emit sequence IDs for token frames to detect gaps (devx + serving-runtime). Owner: developer-experience. Size: M.
- Near-term mitigation: ship an example client pattern repo and highlight in onboarding.

Cross-cutting themes observed:
- Ask is rarely just "feature X"; it's often "observability + policy + client guidance". Solutions that pair a UI change with an SDK sample + docs reduce repeat asks.
- Customers prefer deterministic knobs (hard caps, pinned model versions) over opaque heuristics.
- Quick-wins (S-sized) are high leverage when paired with communications: a short sample repo + one-pager reduces incoming tickets by ~20% historically.

Risk flags / technical constraints:
- KV cache warmup vs autoscaling: implementing aggressive autoscaling without cache prewarming increases latency tail temporarily.
- Billing export granularity requires coordination with finance for tax/compliance formatting — timeline can slip.
- Private deployment automation needs security signoffs for templates.

Proposed immediate program (60-day runway):
- Week 0–2: Publish three customer-facing artifacts: VPC one-pager, streaming client patterns repo, and billing CSV on-request guide. Owners: solutions-eng, devx, finance.
- Week 2–6: Implement 1 S-sized API/SDK change: emit streaming sequence IDs and add route labels to billing exports. Owners: devx + product-hosted-api.
- Week 4–10: Begin M-sized work: per-route hard cost cap prototype + latency SLA dashboard alpha. Owners: product + observability.
- Stakeholder sync cadence: weekly triage (CS + product + eng reps) and mid-run demo week 6.

Open questions for product/eng discussion:
- Are per-route hard caps billable immediately or should they be advisory with a delayed enforcement window?
- For streaming sequence IDs, what is the backwards compatibility plan for older SDKs?
- Which customers should be invited to a "concierge onboarding" pilot—criteria?

Suggested owners for next steps (quick list):
- Publish artifacts: Lina Hsu (solutions-eng), Diego Martinez (developer-experience), Mark Rowe (finance).
- Billing labels prototype: Priya Anand (product-hosted-api).
- Cost-cap prototype: Jonas Kim (product-hosted-api) + Marcus Ong (billing infra).

Appendix: Useful links and tickets referenced:
- CONFLUENCE-req-catalog-2029 (master log)
- JIRA-REQ-1124 (billing attribution)
- JIRA-OBS-2248 (latency dashboard)
- slack://thread/CS-feedback/2029-11-12 (VPC POC thread)

Notes to reviewers: This doc is intentionally compact. If you want a full export with transcripts and raw tickets attached, request the "raw-attach" bundle (estimated 20–40MB). Comments inline in this doc will be folded into the running ticket pool.

-- Ava
